plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is grown for ornament, oil, and seeds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across Europe, Asia, and the Americas
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a movement called heliotropism, but mature blooms settle facing east and stop moving.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower of meadows, roadsides, and prairies that produces dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flowers. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects. The real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like lilac-pink flowers without any leaves present. The foliage appears in spring and dies back by summer, which gives the plant its other name, naked ladies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid. It is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. It blooms at the end of the southern winter and is a hardy, fast-growing species of Australian woodlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated every year on September 1.
